prerequisites: It is recommended to have passed the course Materials Science and Technology from the second year.

learning_outcomes.text: To know the most appropriate production and processing technologies for different materials depending on the part to be produced, and of the desired in-service properties.
To understand the relationships between processing and the final structure obtained from materials, and their influence on mechanical properties and those associated with their in-service behavior.

To know and understand the different failure mechanisms of materials in service, in-service inspection techniques using destructive and non-destructive tests, and the basic methodology for failure analysis and report preparation.
To know the latest trends in materials of interest for Mechanical Engineering, along with their production and recycling processes, properties and applications.

syllabus_topics: Topic 2.- Structure and properties. Design, cost, and availability
Topic 6.- Synthesis of polymers. 3D printing. Design and characterization.
Practice 3.- Mechanical consequences of cold work.
Practice 4.- Recrystallization treatment against work hardening
Practice 5.- Heat treatments of steels. Microstructural evolution.
Topic 10.- Corrosion and degradation of materials
Topic 11.- Fracture, fatigue, creep. Friction and wear. Failure analysis.
Advanced Materials Seminar, which will be conducted in English and students will submit their report or assignment in that language.
teaching_methods: Practical classes in the classroom (exercises and theoretical-practical cases, discussions)
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade is calculated as 0.1*Personal Work + 0.1*Oral Presentation + 0.2*Laboratory Practices + 0.6*Partial Exams. A minimum of 5 out of 10 is required in each partial exam to average them. To pass the course, at least 80% of lab practices must be completed and their reports approved, and a minimum of 5 must be obtained in the Partial Exams (EXA) component. If lab practices are not passed but the written exam (EXA) is passed, the final grade will be a fail (3.4). The single assessment mode (for second call or renouncing continuous assessment) consists of a Theoretical Exam (80%) and a Practical Exam (20%), with a minimum grade of 5.0 required in both to pass.
